notes: Both coders found the same three university-layer documents (Policy 100-022, Provost initial guidelines, CETLA AI page) and set stance to delegates on all three (CETLA tiers listed); no school, computing or course documents. Main disagreements: (1) phase for standing rules (data entry bans, 'when in doubt', Provost principles) coded general vs during-work, resolved as general when the rule applies to all use and during-work when it attaches to doing the work (research documentation, disclosure, checking output); sample syllabus text resolved as course-start; (2) modality should vs must for the CETLA responsibilities list, resolved as must where the item restates a 'shall' in Policy 100-022 (communicate in syllabus, follow course rules, ask when unsure, verify, disclose when required) and left should for advisory items and checklists; informs vs must-not/may for tier labels and consequence sentences ('may constitute a violation'), resolved as informs; (3) policy_type splits: P56 vs P61/UNCOVERED for principle clauses such as 'shall not undermine learning objectives' (P56), P50 vs P65 for 'not used to train AI systems' (P50, data protection), P56 vs P50 for the work-related compliance clause (P56), P05 vs P04 for 'only in the ways authorized by the instructor' and 'uses outside the stated parameters' (P04), P31 vs P32 for 'output should not be treated as automatically accurate' (P31), P17 vs P63 for ETS Copilot training (P63), P07/P63/UNCOVERED for 'develop an awareness of how these programs operate' and AI literacy aims (P44); one UNCOVERED kept, the AI-enabled phishing / report suspicious messages sentence, which is cybersecurity guidance not covered by P50; (4) unit_stance: coders used permit or require for disclosure duties and accountability duties; resolved as neutral because those sentences take no position on whether AI may be used; (5) actor splits (all vs admin vs ta-staff) resolved by who the sentence addresses (e.g. F.2 binds faculty, staff and student employees: all). Only-A units: 7 found, 6 kept (rationale, syllabus-template commitment, recommendation and faculty-support sentences), 1 dropped (historical background about spell checkers as technological aids, not a policy). Only-B units: all 15 kept (definitions of Confidential Information, IP, PII, PHI and University Data; the new-contract review rule; Provost values and recommendation sentences; CETLA purpose, generative AI definition, and the Level 3 documentation-not-required rule). The Provost sentence on clear parameters and on penalties was split into two units (A parameters, B penalties) because they are different rules. new_types empty on both sides, so none merged. Agreement shares are computed on raw coder codes over the 102 matched units; final file has 123 units.
